newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden says Russian plane played part in jet crash.
newsitem.headline: Sweden says Russian plane played part in jet crash.

text.p: The head of Sweden's air force said a Russian plane played a part in the crash on Wednesday of a Swedish fighter jet just metres (yards) from a nuclear-powered Russian warship, but said the accident was unprovoked.

An AJSH 37 Viggen on a surveillance mission crashed into the Baltic Sea about 120 km (75 miles) off the southeast coast of Sweden, missing the warship it was spying on by about 200 metres (660 feet). The pilot was still missing late on Wednesday.
Kent Harrskog, the head of Sweden's air force, told national Swedish news agency TT that a Russian submarine reconnaissance airplane in the vicinity had interfered in the incident.
"Yes, it naturally interfered with the whole thing," TT quoted Harrskog as saying.
"But it was not a question of deliberate provocation from the Russian side."
The Swedish airplane was helping another jet photograph the Russian vessel Pyotr Veliky in international waters.
TT said the vessel was brand new, one of the most advanced in the Russian fleet and on its maiden voyage after being launched earlier this year.
The two Swedish aircraft were flying at low altitude when they saw the Russian plane in front of them, Harrskog said.
The pilot of the plane which crashed had said "we'll go underneath" the Russian plane over the radio to the other Swedish jet a few kilometres (miles) behind him, Harrskog added.
The plane, part of a squadron based at the central Swedish town of Soderhamn, crashed into the water off the Swedish island of Gotland at 1145 GMT.
Witnesses said they did not see the pilot eject and his body has not been found.
Harrskog praised the international rescue squad at the scene after the accident, calling it an example of cooperation.
"Russian and Latvian helicopters and ships helped in the search. It's a good example of how a rescue operation should work in the Baltic," Harrskog said.
Rescue workers in helicopters and ship at the site had recovered the plane's fuselage.
Swedish Armed Forces Lieutenant-Colonel Lars Olin said the aircraft hit the water about 200 metres (660 feet) away from the Russian warship -- witnessed by the vessel's crew.
Russia's Itar-Tass news agency said the ship was en route from St Petersburg to the port of Baltiisk in the western Russian enclave of Kaliningrad when the accident occurred.
Russian navy officials said the Viggen flew over the ship and crashed when the pilot lost control of the plane as he tried to make a sharp right-hand turn at low altitude.
The accident is the third involving Swedish air force Viggens in as many months.
"I don't see any connection between the accidents," TT quoted Harrskog as saying.
On October 10, two air force JA 37 Viggen jets collided in mid-air about five km (three miles) east of the town of Ramesele in central Sweden. Both pilots ejected and were unhurt.
In August, another air force AJS 37 Viggen crashed into the Baltic Sea while on exercises near Ornskoldsvik in northern Sweden. The pilot was killed.
